newsitem.title: USA: Clinton does not consider Dole evil, aide says.
newsitem.headline: Clinton does not consider Dole evil, aide says.

text.p: The White House said on Friday that President Bill Clinton does not consider Bob Dole an "evil man" despite such a characterisation attributed to him in a new book by disgraced political adviser Dick Morris.
"That is factually incorrect," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.

Morris, who resigned as a Clinton political adviser last August in the fallout over a sex scandal, has written a book about presidential politics called "Behind the Oval Office: Winning the Presidency in the Nineties."

It was due out next week but the Washington Post obtained an early copy and quoted Morris as writing that Clinton once screamed at length during the 1996 campaign that the Republican Dole was "an evil, evil man."
Clinton defeated Dole on Nov. 5 to win a second term.

McCurry could not say definitively that Clinton did not make the remark but went to great pains to stress that the president has often expressed his respect and admiration for the ex-senator from Kansas and his public service.

"I was certainly never present when President Clinton said anything like that," he said. "That's not his view and I don't really believe that Dick Morris was ever in a place where President Clinton said something like that because that's not the president's thinking."

Clinton has read through a copy of the book and, according to McCurry, "thinks parts of it are interesting, parts of it are wrong, parts are factually off the mark, some of it provides insight. He thought Dick made an attempt to be fair in some of the characterisations."
